lede: The week's defining signal: luxury consumers are already inside AI search — and brands that haven't cracked GEO are being outranked by specialists a tenth of their size.

stories.headline: Bain & Comité Colbert: 82% of Top Luxury Spenders Use AI in Their Purchase Journey — GEO Is Now the Battleground
stories.summary: The fifth annual Bain/Comité Colbert Luxury & Technology report drops a structural alarm: luxury consumers are adopting AI for discovery, comparison and purchase at a pace that leaves maisons trailing. 82% of very-heavy spenders used AI in Q1 2026, yet fewer than 20% of luxury executives report significant AI impact internally. The sharpest finding for media teams: 70% of AI searches don't mention a brand name, and 90% of LLM signals come from offsite sources — customer reviews, editorial, blogs — not brand.com. Bain's Nathalie Remy frames GEO as the defining media battle: 'Being big, powerful, and wealthy is no longer enough to emerge in AI search.'

stories.headline: First AI Luxury 25 Index: Hermès Scores 98.6 — Brand Coherence Is Now a Measurable Performance Asset
stories.summary: 5W AI Communications and Haute Living released the first-ever ranking of luxury houses by AI-engine clarity, scoring 25 maisons across ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Perplexity, and Google AI Overviews. Hermès leads at 98.6 — its single unbroken narrative, zero licensing sprawl and no sub-brand noise mean every engine returns the same identity. The structural implication for conglomerates is pointed: LVMH and Kering houses that have cycled through creative directors or operate across fragmented sub-brand identities are structurally more exposed to the ambiguity the index penalises. The methodology rewards the same thing heritage luxury was always built on — consistency over time — but now that consistency has a score.

stories.headline: Every Major Ad Holding Company Is Now Racing to Rebuild Itself as an AI Operating System
stories.summary: Storyboard18's definitive analysis of the 2026 holdco landscape confirms the industry has passed the point of 'AI as feature' — Publicis, WPP, Omnicom, Havas and Dentsu are each restructuring their core operating model around AI infrastructure, proprietary data, and identity resolution. Publicis leads with its $2.2B LiveRamp acquisition layered onto Epsilon and Marcel. Omnicom is integrating Acxiom's Real ID and Flywheel into its Omni platform post-IPG merger. WPP's Elevate28 plan targets £500m in savings by collapsing its holding structure entirely. The implication for luxury media buyers: your agency partner's AI stack is now a material procurement variable — not a pitch-deck claim.

stories.headline: Bain-Comité Colbert Primary Data Drop: AI Priority Jumps From 5% to 22% at Top Luxury Houses in Two Years — But Only 9% Have Deployed at Scale
stories.summary: The primary press release from the Bain/Comité Colbert 5th annual Luxury & Technology report gives the raw data behind this week's biggest luxury AI story. AI has jumped from 5% to 22% as a top-3 corporate priority at luxury houses in just two years — but the execution gap is stark: only 9% of luxury houses have deployed AI for client advisor assistance at scale with measurable impact, and large-scale deployment remains concentrated in back-office support functions (6% in 2024 to 31% in 2026). The report formally identifies GEO as a strategic category for the industry for the first time, noting that luxury maisons are structurally disadvantaged against specialist brands in LLM retrieval.
